# Wiki validation checklist

Use for an approved Wiki outcome. Related existing page/link repairs may be chosen within that outcome; a projected maintenance inventory is not an exact whitelist. Record actual changed paths and material scope decisions.

## Scope and location

- [ ] For maintenance, confirm changed pages and nearby index/link repairs are necessary to the approved documentation outcome, preserve unrelated user content and do not introduce new requirements or a guessed Wiki root.
- [ ] For **creation**, confirm the engineer explicitly selected an exact repository-contained non-lifecycle parent; derive exactly `<selected-parent>/Wiki/`, not an inferred `docs/` default. Creation scope identifies page/index/navigation intent; created Wiki targets stay inside that root. A missing parent may be created only if explicitly selected.
- [ ] Do not create a parent, Wiki root or target in `docs/planning/`, `docs/delivery/`, a verified `<documentation-directory>/copilot/` lifecycle parent/numbered topic or another lifecycle namespace. RPIR root selection does not choose the Wiki parent.
- [ ] Ask promptly before a material change in audience, requirements, external effects, new root or unsupported source claim; continue independent safe work.

## Reader path and evidence

- [ ] Page purpose, audience, prerequisites, content and next steps are clear with logical headings and readable Markdown.
- [ ] Trace the reader path from the relevant index to the page and onward. Check inbound and outbound links after related-page maintenance, with descriptive text and existing intended targets.
- [ ] Trace material factual claims to canonical repository sources or cited Research evidence; link to policy, lifecycle and packaging truth rather than copying its authority. Correct stale/contradictory claims without inventing facts.

## Validation and report

- [ ] Inspect changed headings, links, sources and navigation manually or with actually permitted checks. Diagnose and recheck ordinary in-boundary failures without a compulsory Runner or command route.
- [ ] Record **Performed**, **Failed**, **Unavailable** and **Not run** separately with outcome/reason; never present unperformed automation or installed behavior as successful.
- [ ] Report actual pages/navigation changed and unresolved factual, accessibility or material-scope gaps; do not introduce hosted integration, publishing or unauthorized external effects.
